junk_imagery.evidence: No photos or AI images; every frame is drawn vector art (dollar-bill bars, circles, a ladder).

decorative_mascot.evidence: In seg2:start through seg2:end Data just perches on top of the $118M circle and reacts. In seg3 he stands on a ladder doing a crossed-arm pose beside the bar. Neither is an action that causes the number.

bare_number_card.evidence: Each beat has a visual. In seg2 the two circles are a basic bubble comparison, but they are more than a bare number.

dead_air.evidence: The measured longest_static_s is 0.0. Bars stack and circles grow across seg0-seg2.

empty_void.evidence: In seg0:start through seg1:end the lower ~35% of the frame below Data is empty dark gradient. In seg3:start most of the frame is empty, with only thin lines and a ladder.

unreadable.evidence: At seg3:end and payoff@-0.4 the label 'Cost to make them $118M' is printed over 'Face value $32M', so '$32M' becomes illegible. At seg3:start the 'Face value $32M' and '$86M apart' labels are low-contrast dim blue on navy.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: At seg3:end and payoff@-0.4 the 'Cost to make them $118M' label overlaps 'Face value $32M', and the two texts collide into an unreadable '$32M'. The scene is a thin bar-and-ladder diagram with large empty space. Data stands on the ladder crossing his arms instead of doing anything about pennies.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The two value labels are placed at the same height without collision measurement. The closing gag ('refuses to pick up pennies') is not staged. Instead a generic gap-ruler machine is reused with Data as a bystander.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Stage the closing as the gag itself. Show a penny on the ground and Data walking past it, or Data picking up a penny that costs 3.69 cents. Lay the two value labels out with measured extents so they never overlap, keep the $86M gap readable, and fill the frame.

depictions.note: Data lifts stacked dollar-bill bars, one stack per year. It is a generic weightlifting stack with no penny anywhere. The stack height does not visibly track the 1.2→3.7 cents (it shrinks in 2015), so the cost rising is not felt.
Same bill-stack lift continued to 3.7 cents. Bars pile up, but nothing shows the cost against a 1-cent face value.
Bubble comparison of $118M vs $32M. The size ratio reads, but it is a plain bubble chart with Data perched on top.
Gap ruler on posts with a ladder. Generic, sparse, and the labels collide. Nothing about pennies.

grades.one_line: A generic dollar-bill weightlifting stack and a bubble chart, with no penny in sight, a static perched mascot, and a closing scene whose labels collide into an unreadable mess.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3) opens on Data holding two bill bars with a dim '2006 1.2' readout. It has no penny, no unit ('1.2' what?) and no reason to stay.
seg0-seg1: the bill stack does not scale with the cost (it drops from 4 bars to 2 at 2015/2020), so the 'every year more' claim is not shown. The bottom third of the frame is empty.
seg2: a plain two-bubble chart. Data just stands on the big circle with his hands up, a decorative reaction.
seg3: 'Cost to make them $118M' is printed over 'Face value $32M' (seg3:end, payoff@-0.4), so the label cannot be read.
seg3: a sparse ruler/ladder diagram with most of the frame empty. The closing gag about refusing to pick up pennies is never shown.
The subject (a penny) never appears in any frame.
fixes: Make the penny the hero. For seg0/seg1, Data feeds 3.69 cents of zinc/copper into a press that stamps out a single 1-cent coin, with the cost pile growing each year.
Hook: open on a penny being minted with a price tag ticking past 1 cent within the first second.
seg2: show $118M as a mountain of minting cost beside a $32M pile of pennies, with Data shovelling into the larger one.
seg3: measure the label extents and stack them so they do not overlap. Stage the actual gag: Data steps over a penny on the ground.
Fill the lower third of the frame in seg0-seg1, either by placing the action lower or by adding a ground/penny pile.
